p: Cheshire Oaks is about much more than shops, and a round of adventure golf is just one piece of the puzzle. Blue Planet Aquarium is right in the same area, with sharks, rays and an underwater tunnel, so it's an easy pairing for a family day. Down in the old docks, the National Waterways Museum tells the story of Britain's canals, with historic boats and the chance to learn how the network shaped the country. And Chester Zoo is just a short drive away for a full-on animal adventure.

For the golf, a few pointers. Read each hole before you take your shot, because a gentle putt with the right angle off the side usually beats a big swing. Watch how the ball behaves on the first couple of holes and adjust. And don't forget the golden rule of crazy golf: whoever's losing gets to make the trickiest hole "not count".

It's worth agreeing on a maximum number of shots per hole before you start, especially with young children. It keeps the round moving, avoids meltdowns and stops anyone getting stuck forever behind the same obstacle.
The whole site is under cover and flat, so it's an easy one for buggies and grandparents alike. Plenty of food nearby means you can play, eat and keep going without needing to move the car.
